stories.headline: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Likely to intensify into severe cyclonic storm today, IMD says
stories.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Likely to intensify into severe cyclonic storm today, IMD says
stories.summary: The system has changed its track slightly, and the probable landfall points may remain between Visakhapatnam and Nellore on November 20
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclonic storm Akvan over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal may intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday morning (November 18, 2026), and further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning (November 19, 2026).

Initially, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast that the weather system would strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening (November 17, 2026), but the system had either remained stationary or moved slowly.

The Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved slowly northwards with the speed of 03 kmph during past 06 hours and lay centered at 2330 hours IST of yesterday, the 17th November, 2026 over the same region, the IMD said in an update early Wednesday.
The system has changed its track slightly, and the probable landfall points may remain between Visakhapatnam and Nellore.

Isolated heavy rainfall is likely in the northern districts of Visakhapatnam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam, Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, and strong winds with speeds of 100 kmph to 110 kmph are likely along the coastal belt from Wednesday evening (November 18, 2026).
Andhra Pradesh is experiencing a very rare event, since it is not often that a State sees three tropical cyclones crossing its coast within a month, said IMD Director General of Meteorology.

“The Cyclonic Storm “Akvan” [Pronunciation: Akvan] over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal moved slowly north-northwestwards with the speed of 03 kmph during past 06 hours and lay centred at 2030 hours IST of today, the 17th November, 2026, over the same region,” IMD said on X. “It is very likely to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify further into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal around the morning of tomorrow, the 18th of November.

stories.headline: Congress wants probe into conflicting versions in Kishtwar incident : Karra
stories.title: Congress wants probe into conflicting versions in Kishtwar incident : Karra
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 17: Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra on Tuesday reiterated that his party wanted probe into conflicting versions vis-a-vis two SPOs' killings in Kishtwar. “Congress objects to the way the BJP has questioned the integrity of Jammu and Kashmir Police (JKP) and used inappropriate words against it. They termed JKP as inefficient and good for nothing which brought down the morale of the entire force (JKP). Secondly, we object to the statements (of BJP leaders) referring to Masjid (mosque). We perceive these statements as attempts aimed at vitiating the atmosphere ahead of Punjab elections,” Karra alleged, while responding to media queries on the sidelines of a party function in Jammu. “You (media) need to ask them (BJP) leaders under what circumstances they made such statements which not only vitiated the atmosphere there (in Kishtwar) but would leave its impact across J&K,” he maintained. Responding to his (Karra's) statement that “SPOs had gone for hunting and were killed in the firing by Army probably due to mistaken identity”, JKPCC president denied having made any statement against the Army. “We did not raise any question about the Army. But what about the charges, they (BJP) have levelled against the Police. We only said that two versions emanated from there (Kishtwar) - one related to militants' angle and the second one related to the Army. We did not level any allegations. We simply said that it was the matter for investigation and all angles should be investigated,” Karra clarified. He also questioned the earlier claims of the central government declaring “Kishtwar-militancy free.” In response to a question about the Kulgam terror attack, followed by an encounter wherein a terrorist was killed, JKPCC president said that the questions on that account should be posed to Centre, MHA, Union Home Minister and the Prime Minister.

stories.headline: Thank you, Geethu: Malta PM praises Malayali nurse in parliament budget speech
stories.title: Thank you, Geethu: Malta PM praises Malayali nurse in parliament budget speech
stories.summary: During his budget address, Malta Prime Minister Robert Abela publicly thanked Keralite nurse Geethu Louis, praising her exceptional pandemic leadership and dedicated healthcare service to his family.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In a heartfelt gesture highlighting the dedication of Indian healthcare professionals abroad, Malta Prime Minister Robert Abela expressed deep gratitude to a Keralite nurse during his budget address in parliament.
Commending her commitment, the Prime Minister acknowledged the crucial role foreign workers play in the nation’s growth and public welfare.
"When my father and mother fell ill, and when my daughter needed care, it was a foreign nurse who came to our aid.
Her name is Geethu.
Thank you, Geethu, we are indebted to your service," Prime Minister Abela remarked during his parliamentary speech.
The nurse, 35-year-old Geethu Louis, hails from Meloor near Chalakudy in Thrissur district.
Prior to moving to Malta in 2018, she worked as an operation theatre nurse in Keralam.
Her journey in the European nation took a pivotal turn during the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, when authorities sought healthcare workers willing to screen incoming passengers at the airport.
While many hesitated, Geethu stepped forward to take on the task.
Recognising her efficiency and courage, officials eventually entrusted her with leading Covid-19 testing operations across the country.
In this leadership role, she managed around 300 healthcare personnel across 32 hospital facilities, establishing herself as one of the most respected healthcare workers in Malta's government network.
Her exceptional reputation led to a personal assignment when former Malta President George Abela, the father of Prime Minister Robert Abela, suffered an injury in an accident.

stories.headline: Tenders, Environmental Laws, and Design Thinking Approach
stories.title: Tenders, Environmental Laws, and Design Thinking Approach
stories.summary: For several generations Mohammad Akbar has been catching fish from Sukhnag stream. This 64 year fisherman from Arwah village in Beerwah tehsil of Central Kashmir’s Budgam District has been into this profession for last more than 40 years. He has inherited it from his parents and grandparents. Sukhnag stream is known for its trout and traditional Kashmiri fish and has been designated as a trout stream by J&K Fisheries Department. Sukhnag is a tributary of the Jhelum, originating from the glaciers of the Pir Panjal mountains and flowing through many villages of Beerwah. For last 5 to 6 years the livelihood of Mohammad Akbar and many other fishermen has been directly impacted? The catch is less as there has been large scale riverbed mining taking place in Sukhnag in around one dozen villages. This author fought this mining mafia in National Green Tribunal-NGT. For last almost 2 years the illegal excavation of boulders, sand and gravel with heavy machinery has been halted to a great extent as NGT has imposed ban on this illegal trade from last almost 2 years now. After the mining ban Sukhnag was reviving day by day and population of fish was also growing, but another human induced disaster has snatched livelihood of Akbar and many of his colleagues. Halting Fish Movement ? Around the autumn of 2024 Govt constructed a concrete structure in the middle of Sukhnag at village Makhama which is around 7kms downstream of Beerwah town. The structure was meant for “protection” of abutments of the bridge but this structure has caused huge loss to the fishermen community. The upward movement of fish has been hampered and fishermen like Mohammad Akbar are not even able to catch 1 kg of fish a day? Mohammad Akbar has to take care of 8 members of family which includes his wife and six daughters. He is not able to do other job due to old age? I, along with my colleagues of J&K Climate Action Group-JKCAG, on November 1st 2026 visited Makhama to meet these aggrieved fishermen. We met around two dozen fishermen and they informed us that there are around 200 families who have been impacted. When the construction work was taken up the concerned departments (PWD, R&B) didn’t consult Fisheries Department or Flood control department. Fisheries Department’s official letter to R&B The Assistant Director Fisheries, Budgam wrote an official letter to Executive Engineer R&B Division Beerwah on 3.04.2025 and advised the department not to go ahead with the construction work as this would severely impact the livelihood of fishermen community (Mahigeers). The official communication reads: “As already discussed telephonically, it is once again reiterated that this office has received a representation from the registered fishermen of Circle Beerwa regarding the construction of an embankment in Nallah Sukhnag under the bridge at Makhama Village. In this regard, it is to state that the fishermen residing in the area are wholly and solely dependent on this Nallah for their daily livelihood by means of catching fish. The construction of the said embankment will definitely result in declining fish production by way of hindering the fish movement upstream, thereby jeopardizing the livelihood of the fishermen. The construction of an embankment across the river will prove very detrimental for the breeding and sustainability of the fish fauna as per the Fisheries regulations. Pertinent to mention here that the only source of income to these fishermen comes from the catch of fish in the Nallah, and if their genuine demand is not considered seriously, it will badly affect their livelihood and also the sustainability of the river “ The R&B Division also didn’t get a No Objection Certificate-NOC from concerned Flood Control Department. I spoke to Mr. Javed Kurpal, Executive Engineer of the Flood Spill Channel Division Narbal, and he confirmed that NOC was not given by them for the construction. Flawed Notice Inviting Tender -NIT I am unable to understand why the Notice Inviting Tenders-NITs are flawed on many occasions as environmental aspect is not taken into consideration. Early this year the authorities had planned to cut down almost 200 mulberry trees on canal road Rawalpora and further ahead upto Pirbagh. The R&B Division Rajbagh Srinagar in December 2025 had invited tenders for Widening and Upgradation of Bund Road (Canal Avenue) from Mochwa Baghe Mehtab to Rawalpora bridge. The contract was allotted on January 24th 2026 to a local contractor on the allotted cost of Rs 1.10 Crores. The work was to be completed in 18 months. Unfortunately the allotment letter or NIT nowhere mentioned environmental aspects of the work ? The tender document as well as contract allotment document was itself flawed as they both violate J&K Preservation of Specified Trees Act 1969 wherein cutting down of Mulberry tree is completely banned. The Jammu and Kashmir Mulberry Protection Act, 1949 also prohibits cutting of these trees and the way permission was granted to axe 62 trees needs to be investigated. I had written a detailed piece on that, and uploaded videos on social media as well. The work was halted but in Pirbagh area the trees are now choked in concrete. No Empathy for Fishermen? Similarly, if the R&B Division has plans to protect abutments of Makhama bridge, why didn’t they think of Fishermen community? Why didn’t they respect the National Water Policy and J&K Water Resources (Regulation and Management Act ) Act 2010. Both of them have been violated. The fact of the matter is that engineers hardly visit the site. The contractor does what he wants. When Fishermen resisted, contractor got them booked and they were put inside the lockup. Our Govt talks about “Design Thinking” which is now part of our National Education Policy. The core value of Design Thinking is based on Empathy and this is missing in our Govt sector especially when we execute the Govt works on the ground? Empathy is the core starting point of design thinking. It is the practice of understanding the people you are designing for, setting aside your own assumptions, and seeing the world through their eyes. I ask the Executive Engineer R&B Division Beerwah; did you prepare the NIT of Makhama bridge using Design Thinking principles? Why was empathy towards Fishermen missing? Minister Intervenes This author has taken up this matter with Hon’ble Agriculture Production Minister Mr Javaid Ahmad Dar, who also holds portfolio of Fisheries Department. He responded to my request promptly and asked the Director Fisheries J&K Govt Mr Abdul Majeed Tak to take legal action against the R&B Engineers and the Contractor. The Fisheries Department issued a fresh letter asking Executive Engineer R&B Beerwah to address the issue and remove the structure. This is not enough; the Fishermen who have been impacted for last almost 2 years should be compensated as well by the government. Conclusion I appeal authorities especially Chief Engineers of PWD (R&B), PHE Irrigation, UEED, and KPDCL to make sure they prepare all the NITs in consonance with Environmental Laws and by respecting the design thinking principles- especially empathy, ideation and multi-disciplinary approach. The Engineering Departments especially must consult environmental experts while preparing tender documents (NITs). Furthermore, all engineering construction divisions must have an Environmental Engineer or Environmental Consultant position to examine the tender documents before they are issued. Dr Raja Muzaffar Bhat is an Acumen Fellow. He is Chairman J&K Climate Action Group & Founder of J&K RTI Movement

stories.headline: How Youth and Communities Are Coming Together to Protect Kashmir's Vital Water Commons
stories.title: How Youth and Communities Are Coming Together to Protect Kashmir's Vital Water Commons
stories.summary: River Jhelum, Foot Bridge Srinagar Submerged ankle-deep in the muddy shallows of the Jhelum, Nayeem Farooq pulled a tangled plastic sheet from the water and dropped it into the growing pile beside him. The B-Tech student from Baramulla had begun cleaning the river only two months earlier. Behind him, volunteers carried sacks of waste up the slippery embankment. For Farooq, the river was no longer just a waterway at the edge of town; it had become a responsibility he could no longer ignore. Nayeem farooq and his team collecting the garbage from the Jhelum in polythenes “The Day the Jhelum Became Personal” “I and my cousin were once sitting on the banks of the Jhelum in Baramulla when he went for a swim in the river. But when he returned, his eyes had turned red. Concerned, I asked him what had happened, and he told me that the polluted water had caused irritation and infection. What seemed like an ordinary moment soon became a deeply disturbing experience for me. There is a need to develop a stronger sense of civic responsibility so that cleanliness becomes a daily habit rather than remaining limited to official drives.
